purpose: Compare period/genre features with nearby papal authors so the style model uses contemporary Catholic prose but does not falsely ascribe conventions uniquely to Giuseppe Sarto.

comparisonDocs.author: Leo XIII
comparisonDocs.title: Mirae Caritatis
comparisonDocs.limitation: Leo XIII speaks on Eucharistic devotion, so differences in subject matter are not differences in personality.

comparisonDocs.author: Benedict XV
comparisonDocs.title: Ad Beatissimi Apostolorum
comparisonDocs.limitation: The 1914 European-war context alters emphasis; this comparison demonstrates genre conventions, not differences in courage or charity.

periodConventionsNotEvidenceOfDistinctiv: Frequent formal first-person plural in papal encyclicals
Venerable Brethren and Apostolic Benediction salutation/closure
Scripture allusions and prolonged periodic syntax
Solemn language about divine providence and the Church's mission
General paternal affection and concern for the salvation of souls

candidateSartoSignalsNeedingRepeatedInte.distinction: Insistence on careful brevity, work of instruction, and concrete concern over learner burden.
Specific coupling of rejecting distorted words or error with charity towards the erring.
Recalls poor rural churches and addresses workaday education/organisation issues in concrete terms.

trainingContract: Sample language forms from nearby period controls for calibration ONLY. Never present Leo XIII or Benedict XV wording as St Pius X's words. Claim Pius-specific tendencies only when attested in his own documents. A two-control sample cannot establish statistical uniqueness.
